title: 07 Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and Diagonalization: Visual Guide
outline: Title: 07 Eigenvalues, Eigenvectors, and Diagonalization — Visual Guide

1. Arrows That Stay | BRIDGE from linear transformations and matrix-vector multiplication: spin an input arrow through 360 degrees for a chosen 2x2 matrix and watch the output, drawn beside it, with the coordinate-mixing arithmetic spelled out row by row and the angle between the two arrows read out live; the dashed green lines are the eigen-directions, and a snap button jumps to the nearest one. | Almost every direction gets turned; an eigenvector is a direction the map only rescales, and the eigenvalue is that scale factor and nothing else — the rotation preset has no real eigen-direction at all.

2. Slide Lambda To Zero | The characteristic equation as a hunt: slide lambda from -2 to 6 and watch det(A - lambda I) traced as a curve, with the shifted matrix, the polynomial lambda^2 - trace*lambda + det, the live determinant, the singular/invertible verdict and the trace and determinant checks all updating. | Eigenvalues are exactly the lambdas where the determinant hits zero, because only a singular A - lambda I admits a nonzero v; the rotation preset's curve never touches the axis, and the repeated-root preset shows both roots landing together.

3. Free Columns To Basis | Eigenspaces are null spaces: pick one free column, two free columns or none, drag the RREF entries of A - lambda I, and watch the row equations, the rank, dim E = 3 - rank and the special-solution basis rebuild themselves, with the RREF times the basis substituted back to confirm it returns the zero vector. | The signs flip when you solve the row rather than read it, one special solution comes per free variable, and an RREF of the identity means that lambda is not an eigenvalue at all rather than a small eigenspace.

4. Two Multiplicities Compared | Algebraic vs geometric multiplicity: choose a characteristic polynomial, then drag each eigenvalue's geometric multiplicity between 1 and its algebraic multiplicity and watch the filled and missing direction squares, the geometric sum against n, and the diagonalizable verdict flip. | Diagonalizable exactly when the geometric multiplicities sum to n; one shortfall settles it however healthy the other eigenvalues, geometric is the nullity of A - lambda I and never its rank, and the algebraic column always totals n so summing it proves nothing.

5. Build P And D | Diagonalization in the open: eigenvectors are computed into the columns of P and eigenvalues into D, with P inverse, D^k, P D^k P inverse and A^k from k actual matrix products shown side by side and compared; a swap button reorders P's columns and D follows, and one preset has only a single independent eigenvector so det P is zero. | AP = PD gives A = P D P inverse, powers cost one line instead of k products, D's entries must match P's column order, and the repeat that supplies too few directions leaves P singular with nothing to invert.

6. Variance And Steady State | Application: PCA on the left, dragging the entries of a 2x2 covariance matrix while the data cloud, its ellipse and the two principal directions redraw with the variance share; PageRank on the right, stepping a 3-page random walk from three different starting distributions and watching the bars converge onto the dashed steady state with the distance from Pv = v shown. | PCA takes the eigenvector of the LARGEST eigenvalue because that eigenvalue is the variance in its direction and the eigenvalues sum to the trace; PageRank takes the eigenvector for lambda = 1, the long-run probabilities of each state, and every start converges to the same equilibrium.
